mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the model to construct an Operation where a non-owner member performs OpPatchTask or OpDeleteTask on a task they do not own. This directly violates FR-008/FR-009 and the OwnershipBasedAccess predicate, which requires that every such operation be performed by the owner or an admin.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipViolation { some op: Operation, t: Task | op.op_kind = OpPatchTask and op.op_actor_role = MemberRole and t in op.op_task and t.task_owner != op.op_actor }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact dissolves the one-to-one binding between Operations and AuditEntries. The injected violation creates two Operations both claiming the same AuditEntry, which simulates a 'reuse/rewrite' of an audit record — exactly the mutation that the append-only invariant forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj op1, op2: Operation, ae: AuditEntry | ae in op1.op_audit_entry and ae in op2.op_audit_entry }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets the model place an Operation that targets a task whose team differs from the operation's team. The injection explicitly constructs such a cross-team access, violating the byte-equivalent 404 isolation invariant central to FR-014 and SC-004.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamViolation { some op: Operation, t: Task | t in op.op_task and t.task_team != op.op_team }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the requirement that PostTask and DeleteTask operations produce exactly one audit entry. The injection creates a PostTask operation with no associated audit entry, modelling the SC-007 failure mode where a task change has no corresponding audit trail entry.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingAuditEntry { some op: Operation | op.op_kind = OpPostTask and no op.op_audit_entry }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the composite-PK uniqueness constraint allows a user to hold two different roles in the same team simultaneously. The injection creates exactly this scenario, which would let a member claim admin privileges in the same team — violating the per-team single-role invariant of FR-007.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DualRoleViolation { some disj m1, m2: TeamMembership | m1.tm_user = m2.tm_user and m1.tm_team = m2.tm_team and m1.tm_role != m2.tm_role }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a task to carry an assignee who is not a member of the task's team. The injection creates a task whose assignee belongs to a different team, directly violating the FR-012 same-team-assignee constraint and the ValidationBeforeMutation predicate.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AssigneeTeamViolation { some t: Task, u: User, tm: Team | u in t.task_assignee and tm != t.task_team and (some m: TeamMembership | m.tm_user = u and m.tm_team = tm) and (no m2: TeamMembership | m2.tm_user = u and m2.tm_team = t.task_team) }
